case_name: Ashok Singh Pal vs Smt. Manjulata
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed application under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act for dissolution of marriage. Respondent filed applications under Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act and Section 125 of Cr.P.C. seeking maintenance pendente lite and expenses. Trial court granted Rs. 1,000/- as maintenance and Rs. 500/- as litigation expenses.

legal_principles.principle: Remedies available under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act and Section 125 of Cr.P.C. are independent.
legal_principles.held: Rejection of application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C. is not a bar for granting maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
cited_cases: Virendra Kumar v. Santosh Dev, (1988) {1} HLR 373

legal_principles.principle: An order granting maintenance under Section 488, old Cr.P.C. does not oust the jurisdiction of the Court to order maintenance under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: It has been held by the Gujrat, Punjab and Haryana and Andra Pradesh High Courts in various cases that a application for temporary alimony under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act is not a bar merely because an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. is also allowed.
cited_cases: Ramesh Chandra v. Dhiraj Gowri, (1982) HLR 455 {Guj}
Devinder Kumar v. Asha Rani, (1988) {2} HLR 452 {P & H}

outcome.final_order: Interim alimony granted by trial court adjusted.

use_for_drafting: seeking maintenance pendente lite in family court
challenging an order of the Family Court
